lines.trans: Music rehearsal starts soon, so Seung-chan, today you are in charge of performer standby.
Two songs before each singer's turn, bring them from the dressing room to stand by right here.
And check that their microphones are clipped on and explain their exit route.
Yes, senior!
I double-checked the entire VIP route flawlessly from the parking lot right to their assigned seats!
Handle that on your own—stop reporting every little thing like that to me!
Let's step out for a quick bowl of black-bean noodles—once rehearsal starts we will have zero time.
No thanks—our crew will just order sandwiches or something later.
Go check what time Cindy is arriving.
Right away, senior!

meanings.note: Indicates that something will happen in a very short time.

examples.trans: The bus will arrive soon.
I will contact you again soon.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 음악이라도 들으시면 잠이 잘 오실 거예요.
examples.trans: If you listen to at least some music, you should fall asleep more easily.
Here the word for 'even just music' is key.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'rehearsal', commonly used in broadcasting and performing arts.

examples.trans: There is a rehearsal before the performance.
The rehearsal starts at 2 p.m.

meanings.note: used both transitively and intransitively

examples.trans: The meeting is starting soon.
I started studying Korean.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 곧 음악 리허설 시작하니까 승찬아, 너는 오늘 스탠바이 담당이야.
examples.trans: Music rehearsal starts soon, so Seung-chan, today you are in charge of performer standby.
Here the word for 'standby' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: Her assigned producer? That pancake guy from last time?
Here the word for 'in charge, assigned' is key.

meanings.note: reflexive pronoun referring back to the subject

examples.trans: You have to look after your own rice bowl.
Do your own work yourself.
Do you know any of my songs?
The topic of song came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Attributive form of 둘 used directly before counter nouns (두 개, 두 사람).

examples.trans: Please give me two apples.
Let's meet at two o'clock.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 꼭 하라는 곡은 빼고 망한다고 빼라는 곡은 타이틀곡으로 하고!
examples.trans: They drop whichever song he loves and make whichever song he says will flop their title track!
Here the word for 'song' is key.

examples.text: 나 마음 바뀌기 전에 빨리 계약서 보내는 게 좋을 거예요.
examples.trans: You had better send the contract quickly before I change my mind.

examples.text: 게임을 하기 전에 미리 확인을 받으라고? 지금 장난해?
examples.trans: Get approval in advance before every game? Are you kidding me right now?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 자기 노래 두 곡 전에 분장실에서 이쪽으로 스탠바이 시키고,
examples.trans: Two songs before each singer's turn, bring them from the dressing room to stand by right here.
Here the word for 'from the dressing room' is key.
Did you hear about this only to your side?
I was busy today because of only to your side.

meanings.en: to make someone do, to assign work
meanings.note: Causative verb; e.g., 일을 시키다 'to assign work'.
E.g., 치킨을 시키다 'to order fried chicken'.

examples.trans: The team leader assigned this work to me.
Shall we order pizza for dinner?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 마이크 찬 거 확인하고 퇴장 동선도 일러주고.
examples.trans: And check that their microphones are clipped on and explain their exit route.
Here the word for 'microphone' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 마이크 찬 거 확인하고 퇴장 동선도 일러주고.
examples.trans: And check that their microphones are clipped on and explain their exit route.
This expression comes from 'wearing, clipped on'.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
Let's checked together today.
I worked hard to checked yesterday too.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: And check that their microphones are clipped on and explain their exit route.
Here the word for 'stage exit' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 마이크 찬 거 확인하고 퇴장 동선도 일러주고.
examples.trans: And check that their microphones are clipped on and explain their exit route.
Here the word for 'movement path too' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 마이크 찬 거 확인하고 퇴장 동선도 일러주고.
examples.trans: And check that their microphones are clipped on and explain their exit route.
This expression comes from 'explain to them'.

meanings.note: Standard polite affirmative response; also used to acknowledge that one is listening.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Yes, I understand.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 내가 VIP 동선을 주차장에서 지정석 착석까지 완벽하게 다 확인했다!
examples.trans: I double-checked the entire VIP route flawlessly from the parking lot right to their assigned seats!
Here the word for 'VIP' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 내가 VIP 동선을 주차장에서 지정석 착석까지 완벽하게 다 확인했다!
examples.trans: I double-checked the entire VIP route flawlessly from the parking lot right to their assigned seats!
Here the word for 'from the parking lot' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 내가 VIP 동선을 주차장에서 지정석 착석까지 완벽하게 다 확인했다!
examples.trans: I double-checked the entire VIP route flawlessly from the parking lot right to their assigned seats!
Here the word for 'assigned seats' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 내가 VIP 동선을 주차장에서 지정석 착석까지 완벽하게 다 확인했다!
examples.trans: I double-checked the entire VIP route flawlessly from the parking lot right to their assigned seats!
Here the word for 'all the way to seating' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 내가 VIP 동선을 주차장에서 지정석 착석까지 완벽하게 다 확인했다!
examples.trans: I double-checked the entire VIP route flawlessly from the parking lot right to their assigned seats!
This expression comes from 'flawlessly'.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

examples.trans: That is my mobile phone.
That is really important.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Determiner modifying a following noun.

examples.text: 그런 실수는 누구나 할 수 있어요.
examples.trans: Anyone can make a mistake like that.
This is the first time I'm hearing a story like that.

meanings.note: Contracted form of 이야기하다

examples.trans: Let's talk again later.
Please tell me honestly.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

나가다.gloss: to go out, to step outside

meanings.en: to go out, to step outside, to leave a room
meanings.note: 나- ('out') + 가다 ('to go')

examples.trans: Let's step outside for a moment and talk.
He went out of the conference room.
Did you hear about this black-bean noodles?
I was busy today because of black-bean noodles.

meanings.note: Determiner form of 하나, used before a noun counter.

examples.trans: one person
one hour

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 나가서 짜장면이라도 한 그릇씩 먹고 오자, 리허설 시작하면 시간도 없을 텐데.
examples.trans: Let's step out for a quick bowl of black-bean noodles—once rehearsal starts we will have zero time.
Here the word for 'a bowl each' is key.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Available time or duration.
Used with native Korean numbers to count hours (한 시간 = one hour).

examples.trans: Do you have time?
It takes two hours.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.
Did you hear about this since I intend to?
I was busy today because of since I intend to.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 됐어, 우리는 이따가 그냥 샌드위치 같은 거 시켜 먹을게.
examples.trans: No thanks—our crew will just order sandwiches or something later.
Here the word for 'in a little while' is key.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 됐어, 우리는 이따가 그냥 샌드위치 같은 거 시켜 먹을게.
examples.trans: No thanks—our crew will just order sandwiches or something later.
Here the word for 'sandwiches' is key.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: interrogative noun asking about time; combines with particles like -부터 (from)

examples.trans: When did you come to Korea?
Since when have you worked here?
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
